name: Mithril
summary: Mithril provides an AI omnicloud platform intended to make compute more accessible and efficient for AI developers and research teams.
overview: Mithril provides an AI omnicloud platform for developers and research teams. The company says its platform is designed to make compute more accessible across cloud environments while supporting AI workloads.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: Announced as Foundry in March 2024; the business became Mithril in August 2025. Valuation was not disclosed.

bull_case: A unified cloud layer can become valuable if it meaningfully reduces the complexity and cost of acquiring compute for AI workloads.
bear_case: Cloud infrastructure is capital intensive and intensely competitive. Mithril has not publicly disclosed financing, valuation or operating metrics that would support a fuller underwriting case.
latest_round: March 2024: $80M Seed and Series A; valuation undisclosed
directory_notes: Public financing and operating data remain limited.

intelligence.description: An AI omnicloud platform for developers and research teams.

metrics.label: Latest disclosed funding
metrics.note: Seed and Series A; valuation undisclosed

company: Mithril offers an AI omnicloud platform intended to provide developers and research teams with flexible access to compute. The company previously operated as Foundry before adopting the Mithril name.
Its public materials emphasize AI workloads and cross-cloud access, but do not disclose financing, valuation, customers or operating metrics. This profile therefore does not infer commercial scale.
intelligence.why_it_matters: As AI demand grows, developers increasingly need access to scarce and expensive compute. The question is whether Mithril can provide a differentiated layer above hyperscalers and specialized GPU clouds.

valuation_history.round: Seed and Series A, announced as Foundry

changed.text: Foundry announced $80M in Seed and Series A financing; it rebranded as Mithril in August 2025.

takeaways: Mithril is building an AI omnicloud platform for compute access.
The company was previously known as Foundry.
The company announced $80M in Seed and Series A funding; a valuation was not disclosed.
